title: [finding] `spec-property-retirement` skill predates the `live-elsewhere` verdict — its ledger-verdict discipline never names the never-remove cross-repo case
body:
Recorded from the #13483 delivery (PR #14056). Unassigned — recording only, for triage.

## What

`.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` is the internal playbook for ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove and consumes liveness-ledger verdicts ("the ledger says dead", tombstone rows with `status: "dead"`). #13483 added a fifth verdict, `live-elsewhere` — dead here by measurement, genuinely enforced in a sibling repo — precisely so that a dead-here-enforced-elsewhere key can never again be read as a removal input (the `manifest.runtime` near-miss: the cloud marketplace publish gate consumes it, and the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-30 on the #11330 thread ruled retirement out).

## The drift

The skill's discipline ("a `dead` verdict is input, not proof — build your own evidence before deleting") still holds and nothing in it breaks mechanically. What is missing is the vocabulary: a reader following the skill has no line telling them that the cross-repo-consumer case now has its own status, that such a row is NEVER a removal candidate, and that its attestation discipline (foreign pointer + cross-repo scope + dated `verifiedAt` + 180d expiry, `scripts/liveness/elsewhere.mts`) is what to check instead. The ledger README (packages/spec/liveness/README.md, "live-elsewhere" section) is the source to cite.

One or two sentences in the skill's verification-side section suffice. Out of scope for #13483 (the card's surface is the ledger + gate tooling; the skill is a downstream consumer), filed instead per the dispatch order.
